prompt:
Judge this backlog with /bead-refine, in map mode.

Two things are already settled, so ask me nothing and wait for nothing. The purpose is the one README.md states. The milestone table in docs/milestones.md is correct as written, so treat the milestone names as confirmed and set a real route on every bead.

No shell command runs here, so run none, and do not run bd. Read .beads/issues.jsonl instead. Each line of that file is one bead record, in the shape `bd list --json` returns. It holds every bead in the tracker and none of them is closed. To check whether a path exists, read it or list its directory, never with git ls-files or grep.

This backlog holds fewer than eight beads, so skip clustering and judge all of them as one theme named Uploads.

Print the Step 6 round for that theme, then stop. Apply no verdict and change no bead.
why: The Step 6 round is what a product owner reads, and this is the only seam that sees what the skill prints. It grades four things: the table holds the six columns bead tadw-1zh cut it down to and nothing after them, every row carries the route Step 4 set, every Why cell stays at 15 words or fewer, and the moved fields land in the Detail list rather than in a seventh column. The header check ends at the pipe after Why, because a pattern left open there matches a seventh column appended to the row, which is the exact regrowth tadw-1zh was filed to stop. Four decisions have measurements behind them. The prompt forbids bd and every other shell command, because `claude -p` denies the Bash tool without approval, and the `--add-dir` the harness passes grants a directory rather than a tool; the fixture ships the tracker as .beads/issues.jsonl so the model reads the same records `bd list --json` would return. A `tadw-` id is forbidden because that same `--add-dir` puts this repository's own backlog within reach, and a round judging it would satisfy every shape check while judging no bead in the fixture. The case carries no `max_sentence_words`, because the harness splits sentences on `.`, `!`, and `?` alone: the round opens with a heading, a `Judged against:` line, and a `**Detail**` label, none of which end in a period, so they join the first bullet into one 49-word fragment. Measured 2026-09-08 on a correct round, whose longest real sentence was 18 words. The Why-cell width check replaces it, and it measures the rule the skill actually states. Both arms run: bead tadw-3xh asks for a grade on each, and the baseline arm has no skill to follow. Measured 2026-09-08, the baseline printed five columns in a different order, put a milestone name in the Route cell, and used two em-dashes. `acme-` is forbidden because those ids belong to the worked example inside the skill, and copying it would pass every shape check while judging no bead here.

require_regex.why: the round table holds exactly these six columns, in this order, and nothing after Why: the row must end at that pipe, or a seventh column passes unnoticed
at least one Route cell holds a route Step 4 set, not a hyphen: both yardsticks were confirmed in the prompt
the round names a bead from this fixture, so it judged this backlog
idle days moved into the Detail list rather than being dropped with the seven cut columns

forbid_regex.why: a Why cell of 16 words or more; the skill caps that cell at 15 words, because the author reads it in a narrow column beside five others
these are the columns tadw-1zh moved into the Detail list; a header cell holding one means the table grew back
a bead id from the plugin's own tracker; `ask` passes --add-dir for the plugin, so the model can reach this repository and must not judge its backlog instead of the fixture's
these ids belong to the worked example in the skill; the round must judge this backlog, not copy that example
em-dash; the house style forbids it everywhere
